key_insight: Random train/test splits in perovskite-ML benchmark studies can leak duplicated devices and overstate model skill, so provenance-grouped splits are needed to measure true generalization.
engineering_relevance: For device optimization, this protocol helps researchers choose models and evaluate them on realistic unseen institutions and future data, improving confidence in design rules for high-efficiency perovskite solar cells.
method: Mapped institutional provenance in the Perovskite Database.
Built a hierarchy of grouped splits that progressively separates duplicate devices, publications, and institutions.
Benchmarked 13 models across the grouped evaluation settings.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that nearly two-thirds of curated devices have an exact recipe duplicate, meaning random splits mostly test memorization rather than physical generalization.
watch_item: Grouped evaluation may reduce apparent accuracy, so results should be interpreted as more realistic but also more demanding than standard random splits.
paper_title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics
